title: Injection tests of a Gaia DR3 and ZTF dimmer search give a prevalence of about 8e-8 for Gaia20cdd-like deep dust dimming of field dwarfs; the search misses dwarfs that stay faint most of the time
abstract: Deep, aperiodic dust dimming of mature field dwarfs (Gaia20cdd, G2870, G2698) was found by blind searches, but no search had a measured completeness, so no rate existed. We measured the completeness of the published Gaia DR3 + ZTF DR24 search (sci:sha256:e10c5778) with 64,000 injections into 1,000 random stars of its parent sample. We used real Gaia scanning-law epochs, real ZTF light curves and the unchanged selection and classifier. Our rerun reproduces the published counts and all 2,579 ZTF classes. Gaia20cdd-like activity is recovered as a dimmer deeper than 2 mag with probability 0.41. Activity that keeps a star faint most of the time (G2698-like) is recovered at 0.03, because the classifier's median baseline is a dimmed level; G2698 also fails the parallax cut (7.997 < 8). A G2870-like one-off event has an effective window of only 0.12 yr. With one detection among 3.09e7 northern dwarf-band stars, the Gaia20cdd-like prevalence is 7.9e-8 (68 %: 1.4e-8 to 2.6e-7), or 3.0e-7 if the Gaia periodic-class cut removed every processed dimmer. The G2870-like onset rate is 2.7e-7 per star per year. The 3,674 stars that the class cut removed contain no deep long-dip dimmer. A new bright-envelope classifier recovers G2698-like activity at 0.55; it finds no new deep field dimmer (17 of 21 new detections are young stars), so mostly-faint deep dimmers have a prevalence below 2.2e-7 (95 %). If all dwarfs take part, each spends about 560 yr (100-1,800 yr) in the dimming state over 7 Gyr. With the published Gaia20cdd dust supply this needs about 1e25 g of dust per star, near five asteroid belts. Limitations: one or two detections, model dimming histories, an approximate Gaia flux and parallax model, an unmodelled Gaia variability pipeline and no vetting of injections.
